gaps.wanted: WHICH USB GENERATION THE -24, -24P, -48 AND -48P CARRY. The guide's Table of Ports and Port Descriptions give USB 2.0 on those four and USB 3.0 on the -48C/-48CP; the datasheet FEATURES says '2x USB 3.0 Type A' with no SKU split. The one 48-port front figure (captioned for all four 48-port SKUs) prints the SuperSpeed 'SS' mark and the 24-port figure does not. Modelled per the guide table; the front panel's SS legend is drawn on all four 48-port builds because only one 48-port panel exists. A photograph of an ES1000-48 or -48P front closes it.

A way to carry the per-SKU power maximum (<3200 W PoE, <550 W non-PoE), the PoE budget and the CPU per configuration. Today they are device attrs stated for the whole family with the split in words, as on cisco/asr-9001's gap of the same name.

The vendor part numbers of the 550 W, 920 W and 1600 W supplies. Neither the guide nor the datasheet names them, and the ordering table lists only chassis SKUs. Whether the 1600 W supply is the same Gospower G1482-1600WRA already modelled for the ES1010 (celestica/psu-1600@1, drawn from bench photos with a purple latch and one lamp, against this guide's black tab and two lamps) is the open question.

Whether the 550 W supply has one lamp or two. The PSU LEDs table describes one bi-colour lamp for the 550 W and a DC OK / AC OK pair for the 920 W and 1600 W; the rear figures draw two windows on every supply and the guide says the rear of all ES1000 systems is visually identical. A photograph of a 550 W supply closes it.
What the two round bosses left of fan labels 2 and 3 are (light pipes for per-fan lamps, or plugged holes). The guide documents no fan lamps; they are drawn as outlines only.
A mechanical drawing or square-on photographs of the lid, underside and sides. Everything on those faces is placed by proportion from three-quarter renders.
`physical-context` on 2 bays (rear 2); `physical-context` on port groups rj45-1g, sfp28 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: datasheet PHYSICAL DIMENSIONS: height 43.4 mm, width 438.2 mm, depth 371.6 mm. The hardware guide's Key System Specifications gives 371.7 deep; 0.1 mm, recorded here and not filed. Weight 7.6 +/- 0.3 kg with two PSUs (guide). 438.2 is the body between the ear folds: both guide front figures draw the grey ears outside it, and the body measures 438.2 against its own height to 0.1 and 0.4 percent.

fans.note: '2+1 fixed fans' (datasheet); 'three fixed fans' (guide Rear Panel). Not FRUs, so decor plus a region each, as on celestica/es1010. No fan power figure is published.

front-figures.note: GATE 1. Four ES1000 guide figures, all orthographic CAD renders: Front Panels fig 1 (24-port, 1725 x 193, body 1506.5 x 149 px, aspect 10.111 against 438.2/43.4 = 10.097, +0.14 percent, 3.438 px/mm) and its close-up (1537 x 465, body 440.5 px tall, 10.15 px/mm, anchored on the right body edge); fig 2 (48-port, 1421 x 163, body 1247 x 124 px, aspect 10.056, -0.4 percent, 2.846 px/mm) and its close-up (1281 x 365, 7.823 px/mm, byte-identical to the System Status LEDs figure 2). No perspective: the RJ45 wall positions fit one pitch across all four blocks with no drift (block starts 15.8, 107.8, 199.6, 291.7 on the 48-port figure), and the right-hand cluster measured on the two close-ups agrees to 0.5 mm.

legends.note: every legend as printed: port pairs 'N ▲▼ N+1' centred under each column, 1.4 mm tall at baseline 41.7; SFP28 pairs under the bezel; MGMT COMBO with its bracket joining the management SFP and the management RJ45; the arrowhead over the management SFP lamp; IOIOI under the console; STAT, FAN, PWR, ALM set at about 60 degrees beside the lamps; a USB trident under USB 1 and one turned vertical beside USB 2. The 48-port close-up prints the SuperSpeed 'SS' with both tridents, the 24-port close-up does not. The Celestica wordmark is plain text, no logo art. The lug tag is the dark pull-out tab printed ES1000 with LUG TAG under it; it is the seated celestica/lug-tag-ridge-23@1 (the top-ridge card, label ES1000) - see lug-tag.

lug-tag.note: celestica/lug-tag-ridge-23@1 (#700), the top-ridge card in its 23.3 x 3.8 length, label ES1000, at (23.1, 3.1). Re-read on Front Panels figure 1 (3.438 px/mm, 8x grid): the dark slot runs x 23.1 to 46.4 and y 3.1 to 6.9, the lighter ridge along its top edge from about x 26.9 to 43.5 (3.8 to 20.4 in the part's frame, against the part's 3.6 to 19.6), and ES1000 centred on x 34.7; the 48-port figure 2 (2.846 px/mm) agrees within 0.3 mm (slot 22.8 to 46.1, y 3.1 to 7.0). The Foleon es1000-A render shows the same top-edge ridge over ES1000, reading left to right. This replaces the #690 stopgap, celestica/lug-tag@1, whose grip is a block at one end, and closes its lug-tag-lip gap.

port-layout.note: measured on the shared walls of the RJ45 blocks (a flat feature, one per port) on both full front figures: column pitch 13.96 (the 13.97 of std/rj45-ganged@2), block pitch 92.00 (so 8.04 extra between blocks), column 1 centred 15.86 from the left body edge. Both figures agree to 0.2 mm on every wall. Rows: the bright block shell runs y 16.1 to 39.5 with the bar between rows centred at 27.75, so the two 11.0 cells sit at 16.25 and 28.25. Each block is one bright shell 86.8 x 23.4 drawn as panel decor behind its jacks.

port-leds.note: guide Port LEDs table: RJ45 data ports carry a left bi-colour link lamp (green 1000M, amber 10/100M) and a right bi-colour activity/PoE lamp - led-a and led-b of common/rj45-ganged-eth@1, whose windows the figure shows in each housing. The combo RJ45 management port: left bi-colour link, right green activity. Each SFP28 port one bi-colour lamp (green 25G, amber 1/10G) - drawn as the up/down triangles in the band between the stacked cages, which the figures show one per port (the System Status LEDs table's 'two bi-colored LEDs' per SFP28 port disagrees with the Port LEDs table and the drawing; the drawing and the Port LEDs table are followed). The combo SFP management port has one lamp: the green round lamp left of its cage with a printed arrowhead pointing at it.

power.note: guide Key System Specifications, Power Consumption: 'ES1000-24P, ES1000-48P, ES1000-48CP: <3200W, ES1000-24, ES1000-48, ES1000-48C: <550W'. Stated as upper bounds with no ambient or load; filed as max. The per-SKU figure cannot be carried per configuration (config-scoped-device-attrs gap), so the PoE maximum is power-max-w and the non-PoE one power-max-no-poe-w, the edgecore/eps112 spelling. PoE budgets from the guide's power distribution tables: 1550 W (24P, 2 x 920), 2910 W high line / 1710 W low line (48P/48CP, 2 x 1600).

psu.note: guide PSU Power Options and Table of Attributes: 2 x 550 W on the -24, -48 and -48C; 2 x 920 W on the -24P; 2 x 1600 W (1000 W at 100-127 V) on the -48P and -48CP; all F2B and B2F. 'The airflow of the PSUs and Fans must be same F2B or B2F.' The three supplies share one face in every figure, so the three contracts share one skin.

rear-figures.note: ES1000 guide Rear Panel figure 2 (1681 x 182, body 1470 x 145 px, aspect 10.14, +0.4 percent, 3.35 px/mm) is the device's own; the positions are taken off the ES1010/ES1050/EG1050 guide's Rear Panel figure 1 (5736 x 634, 11.5 px/mm), which is the same rear art at 3.4 times the resolution - checked by overlaying both at matched scale (supply edges 256.0/329.5/346.3/419.8, fan centres, labels, all within 0.5 mm). x is taken as a fraction of the body between the outer seams, y as a fraction of its height, because that figure's seams make it 1.7 percent wide against its height. This borrowing is of a sibling guide's figure; the ES1000 figure is the check.

rear-layout.note: three fixed fans behind round honeycomb grilles centred at 50.14, 105.59 and 161.09 (55.47 pitch), y 22.1, about 38.5 across, each labelled with an arrowhead, a fan glyph and its number to its left; two CRPS bays at 256.0 and 346.3 (73.5 x 40), PSU 1 labelled to its left and PSU 2 in the strip at the right edge (arrowhead pointing at it, a boxed lightning glyph, the number); a fixed divider panel 330.2 to 345.6 between the supplies. Left edge: a standoff at the top and two cross-head screws beside an earth symbol - the grounding point; the right strip carries a second earth symbol over one screw. Two round bosses sit left of fan labels 2 and 3; the guide does not say what they are, so they are outlines only. The fan and PSU glyphs are drawn as simple strokes, not traced.

rj45-orientation.note: read off the 24-port close-up at 10 px/mm: every UPPER jack shows its two lamp windows in its TOP corners and its contact comb below the plug bar, every LOWER jack the mirror - windows at the bottom. The lamps sit on the keyway side (common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 which-is-which), so upper jacks are keyway-up (rotate 180) and lower keyway-down (rotate 0), tab-up over tab-down. Same reading on the stacked management jack (windows top, rotate 180) and console (latch notch at the bottom, no windows, rotate 0). NOTE this is the opposite of celestica/es1010's data ports (upper 0, lower 180), which were read off an oblique photograph; the ES1010 guide's own front figure has not been checked against it.

sides-top-bottom.note: no document draws the sides, top or bottom square-on. The three-quarter renders (datasheet page 1, the cls.celestica.com product-page renders) show a plain silver lid with two pressed rounded pads and a label outline, and screws along the sides. Counted from the renders, placed by proportion, every position estimated.

sku-split.note: ONE DEVICE, TWELVE ORDERABLE CONFIGURATIONS. The six SKUs (ES1000-24, -24P, -48, -48P, -48C, -48CP) share one datasheet column (438.2 x 43.4 x 371.6, one weight), one rear ('The rear panel of all ES1000 systems are identical', guide Rear Panel) and one management/uplink cluster, measured identical to 0.5 mm on the 24-port and 48-port close-ups. They differ in front port count, PoE, CPU and supply wattage. PoE-or-not and airflow are configurations as on celestica/es1010 (ES1010-48C and -48CP are configurations of one device there). The 24-port front is a different panel on the same chassis, so it is a VARIANT VIEW (`front-24`, `face: front`) bound by the 24-port configurations - the dell/r740xd precedent, where the 12 x 3.5 in front is `front-lff-12` bound by the lff12 configurations. dcim_export.views_for makes each configuration export only the front it wears.

stack-orientation.note: rule, not a reading: the SFP28 pairs (upper 0 over lower 180) follow the library's belly-to-belly convention (L108). The figures draw the cage lips in the lamp band between the rows, which is what the convention draws; nothing seen overturns it.

uplink-cluster.note: measured on the 24-port close-up (10.15 px/mm) and confirmed on the 48-port close-up (7.82 px/mm): SFP28 2 x 2 bezel 375.0 to 403.6 x 10.5 to 35.1 (28.5 wide = two std/sfp-ganged@1), cages at y 10.5 and 24.7 with a 3.8 mm lamp band between; management SFP cage 355.6 to 370.7 x 2.6 to 12.3 (std/sfp@1 14.5 x 10 centred on it); its lamp centred (352.1, 9.5); USB-A shell 329.1 to 342.2 x 5.5 to 11.4; the stacked management shell 407.0 to 423.6 x 5.4 to 35.4 holding the RJ45 (7.9 to 16.5 opening), USB-A (19.2 to 23.4) and console (26.3 to 35.2); status lamps centred on x 428.79 at y 17.68, 22.71, 27.83, 32.96 (bright-blob centres), 2.5 across; their legends centred on x 425.3. The lamp component is common/led-indicator@1 (a 2 mm lens in a 4 mm box), smaller than the drawn 2.5 lens; right pitch, compromise shape.

usb.note: SOURCES DISAGREE, see the usb-generation gap. The guide's Table of Ports gives USB 2.0 on the -24, -24P, -48 and -48P and USB 3.0 on the -48C/-48CP; the datasheet FEATURES says '2x USB 3.0 Type A' for all. Placements carry the guide's figure for each panel's own art (2.0 on front-24, 3.0 on front, whose figure prints SS) and component-attrs sets 2.0 on usb-1/usb-2 for the -48 and -48P configurations, which also wear std/usb-a@1's usb2 skin (black tongue) through `skins:`; the front-24 placements name that skin directly. The guide notes the ports carry data only, no power.

vents.note: the face is perforated with square holes, and the perforation STOPS at flat metal around every port, lamp and legend. Fields measured on contrast-stretched copies of the two close-ups (10.15 and 7.82 px/mm) and the full 48-port figure: two lattices, 3.2 x 3.2 mm left of the uplinks (holes centred on x 323.9 + 3.2n, y 3.9 + 3.2n) and 4.0 x 3.2 around them (x 374.0 + 4.0n, y 6.65 + 3.2n), drawn as the grille pattern with pattern-pitch and pattern-offset on those lattices; the pattern's holes are about 85 percent of the pitch, larger than the real 2.2 to 2.5 mm. Fields: a top-edge row and the block above RJ45 blocks 1-2 (x 47.5 to 186.5, beside the lug tag); above block 4 to x 325.3 and two rows over the USB on the 48-port panel; on the 24-port panel a left column at 322.2, the two rows over the USB and the full-height field below y 15.3 to x 371.2; around the uplinks a top-edge row, one row between MGMT COMBO and the SFP28 bezel, a block over the status lamps, a column right of them and the bottom rows (under the SFP28 legends from y 37.9, under IOIOI from 40.6). Flat: the USB 1 plate (325.3 to the management SFP, y 4.4 to 15.3), the lamp and management SFP, the MGMT COMBO band, the SFP28 bezel and its legends, the stacked management shell and the lamp column. The 24-port panel is plain metal from x 187 to 322.2 where blocks 3 and 4 would be. The renders show interior parts through the holes in places; those are not drawn.
